title: Naming expectations and ending honestly

captions.physics: Asking directly about each person’s consent
captions.energy: Recognising constraint behind a desired reply
captions.emotions: Feeling wholeness in a clear agreement

meaning: You can find a whole shared answer when strong expectation is named separately instead of replacing freely given consent from both people.
text: Whole consent begins by distinguishing a request from a hidden demand. The Lovers in the physical position of Vishuddha ask about each person’s wish and choose an actual reply. The Devil in energy takes a constructive direction through recognising constraint behind a needed reaction. The World in emotions brings wholeness as the question and its conditions become clear. An honest exchange can feel complete even before every wish is met: actual consent has boundaries and strong expectation need not silently become a shared promise.

For example, you discuss always telling each other personal news first. Clarification reveals a wish for special closeness alongside compulsory priority that both may never have accepted. **A clear outcome distinguishes participation from a binding condition.** You can choose an actual promise to share important things without making the sequence of telling the only measure of trust. Both understand what was accepted and what remains a powerful wish that can be heard without obligatory fulfilment.

The difficulty is seeking an explanation complete enough to settle attachment permanently. Another qualification seems necessary for wholeness while the condition only grows. Accepting a sufficiently clear boundary preserves consent. Completion need not remove every feeling: a wish can have words and a freely given answer retain the right to stand as spoken.
